title: lookout supplied file, version 1
description: What an outside supplier writes for lookout to read: one input's items, already reduced, with the supplier's own account of how the fetch went. A supplier knows nothing about workstreams. lookout asserts every format keyword, which JSON Schema 2020-12 validators skip by default, so enable format validation when checking against this file. The contract is closed: a field it does not list is a violation. Version 1 gains only optional fields, which a lookout built before a field was added refuses, so update lookout before a supplier writes a new one; any other change is a later version with another name.

input.description: The input name the setting's configuration gives this file.

supplier.description: What wrote the file, for a reader tracing a bad reading back to its source.

fetched_at.description: When the supplier last read its source successfully. lookout measures staleness from this.

attempted_at.description: When the supplier last tried. Later than fetched_at means the latest attempt failed.

supplier_status.description: How the supplier's own run went. degraded or error reports a fault, such as a source that refused part of a request; an item lacking a field it has no value for, such as a due date on work that has none, is not one.

reason.description: The supplier's explanation of a degraded or error status, or of its missing_fields, for people.

missing_fields.description: Fields the supplier failed to fill where its source should have had a value, on some items or all, such as one the source withheld. Any entry makes the input degraded. A field an item has no value for by its nature is left off that item and listed nowhere, even when no item in the file carries it, since only the supplier can tell absent from lost.

id.description: Unique within the input, and stable across fetches, so a workstream can name it.

due.description: When the item falls due: a calendar date, or an exact time.

state.description: The source's own state name, free-form, since trackers name their states differently.

attrs.description: Source-specific detail, such as a sprint or an estimate, that has no field of its own.

notes.description: Free text the item was worked under, such as the ticket section of a work container's notes, which lookout searches for the setting's ticket keys. The supplier passes it along without knowing the key pattern. lookout never emits it: only the joins it produces reach a readout. maxLength counts Unicode code points, and one over-long value withholds every item in the file, so a supplier with more text cuts it at whitespace, or leaves the field out, rather than cutting a key in two.
